toolCalls.output:
version: 2.1

parameters:
  setup_go:
    type: string
    default: github.com/circleci-functions/setup-go@v0.5.1-684fd5b

commands:
  setup:
    steps:
      - checkout
      - install-go
      - install-task

  # Installs the toolchain and restores the module, build and lint caches, saved at job end.
  install-go:
    steps:
      - run: circleci run << pipeline.parameters.setup_go >> --
          --version-file go.mod
          --golangci-lint-cache
          --checksum '{{ checksum "go.sum" }}_{{ checksum "clikit/go.sum" }}_{{ checksum "tools/go.sum" }}'
      - run: go version

  install-task:
    steps:
      - run:
          name: Install go-task
          command: |
            sh -c "$(curl --location https://taskfile.dev/install.sh)" -- -d -b "$HOME/.local/bin"
            echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"' >> "$BASH_ENV"

  # GoReleaser's dockers_v2 pipe shells out to `docker buildx build`, so the
  # builder and the registry login have to exist before it runs.
  setup-docker:
    steps:
      - run:
          name: Register QEMU for cross-architecture builds
          # Dockerfile.alpine RUNs `apk add`, once per platform in the manifest,
          # so building its arm64 half on an amd64 host needs binfmt handlers
          # registered. Idempotent, and a no-op for the cimg/base image, which
          # only COPYs.
          command: docker run --privileged --rm tonistiigi/binfmt --install arm64
      - run:
          name: Create a buildx builder
          # The machine image's default buildx driver is `docker`, which can
          # neither build for two platforms in one invocation nor push a
          # manifest list. A docker-container driver can do both.
          command: docker buildx create --use --driver docker-container
      - run:
          name: Log in to Docker Hub
          # Absent on branch dry-runs, which have no context: the snapshot build
          # still exercises the Dockerfile, it just pushes nothing.
          command: |
            if [ -z "${DOCKER_HUB_USERNAME:-}" ]; then
              echo "No Docker Hub credentials — skipping login (snapshot builds do not push)."
              exit 0
            fi
            echo "$DOCKER_HUB_PASSWORD" | docker login --username "$DOCKER_HUB_USERNAME" --password-stdin

  store_results:
    steps:
      - store_test_results:
          path: ./test-reports

executors:
  linux:
    machine:
      image: ubuntu-2604:current
    resource_class: large.gen3

  # Arm64 counterpart to `linux`, for checking both halves of a multi-arch
  # image. Deliberately small: it only pulls and runs a container.
  linux-arm:
    machine:
      image: ubuntu-2604:current
    resource_class: arm.medium

  macos:
    macos:
      xcode: 26.5.0

  windows:
    machine: true
    resource_class: windows.medium

jobs:
  check:
    executor: linux
    steps:
      - setup
      - run: task ci:check
      - store_results

  test:
    parameters:
      executor:
        type: executor
    executor: << parameters.executor >>
    steps:
      - setup
      - run: task ci:test
      - store_results

  mark-release:
    executor: linux
    steps:
      - run:
          name: Plan deployment
          command: |
            circleci run release plan "${CIRCLE_JOB}" \
              --environment-name="default" \
              --component-name="${CIRCLE_PROJECT_REPONAME}" \
              --target-version="1.0.${CIRCLE_BUILD_NUM}-${CIRCLE_SHA1:0:7}"
      - run:
          name: Update deployment status to running
          command: circleci run release update "${CIRCLE_JOB}" --status=RUNNING
      - run:
          name: Update deployment status to success
          command: circleci run release update "${CIRCLE_JOB}" --status=SUCCESS
          when: on_success
      - run:
          name: Update deployment status to failed
          command: circleci run release update "${CIRCLE_JOB}" --status=FAILED
          when: on_fail

  deploy:
    executor: linux
    parameters:
      publish_steps:
        type: steps
        default:
          - run: task ci:release
    steps:
      - setup
      - setup-docker
      - run: sudo apt update --yes
      - run:
          name: Install snapcraft
          command: |
            sudo apt install snapd --yes
            sudo snap install snapcraft --classic
      - run:
          name: Install choco
          command: |
            sudo cp tools/choco.sh /usr/local/bin/choco
            sudo chmod +x /usr/local/bin/choco
            choco help
      - steps: << parameters.publish_steps >>
      - store_artifacts:
          path: dist

  smoke-test:
    parameters:
      executor:
        type: executor
      install-steps:
        type: steps
    executor: << parameters.executor >>
    steps:
      - steps: << parameters.install-steps >>
      - run:
          name: Verify circleci binary
          command: circleci version

  # Matrixed over the executors rather than over the tags: only the architecture
  # needs a machine of its own, so each job checks both variants. Printing the
  # arch inside the container makes the log say which half of the manifest ran. A
  # tag missing this platform fails here anyway — the arm machine images carry no
  # binfmt, so there is nothing to silently emulate an amd64-only image with.
  smoke-test-docker:
    parameters:
      executor:
        type: executor
    executor: << parameters.executor >>
    steps:
      - run:
          name: Verify circleci/circleci-cli:v1
          command: docker run --rm circleci/circleci-cli:v1 sh -c 'uname -m; circleci version'
      - run:
          name: Verify circleci/circleci-cli:v1-alpine
          command: docker run --rm circleci/circleci-cli:v1-alpine sh -c 'uname -m; circleci version'

  docs:
    executor: linux
    steps:
      - setup
      - run:
          name: Generate reference and build the site
          command: task docs:build
      - run:
          name: Check internal links
          command: task docs:test
      - store_artifacts:
          path: docs/website/public
      - persist_to_workspace:
          root: .
          paths:
            - "docs/website/public"

  docs-publish:
    executor: linux
    steps:
      - setup
      - attach_workspace:
          at: .
      - run:
          name: Publish to gh-pages
          command: task ci:docs:publish

  ok-to-deploy:
    type: no-op

workflows:
  ci:
    jobs:
      # gh-pages holds only generated HTML — never run CI on it. Entry jobs (no
      # `requires`) must opt out explicitly; downstream jobs are gated by these.

      - check:
          filters:
            branches:
              ignore: gh-pages

      - test:
          matrix:
            parameters:
              executor:
                - linux
                - macos
                - windows
          filters:
            branches:
              ignore: gh-pages

      - docs:
          filters:
            branches:
              ignore: gh-pages

      - deploy:
          name: dry-run
          publish_steps:
            - run: task ci:build
          filters:
            branches:
              ignore:
                - main
                - gh-pages

      - ok-to-deploy:
          requires:
            - check
            - test
            - docs
          filters:
            branches:
              only: main

      - mark-release:
          requires:
            - ok-to-deploy

      - deploy:
          serial-group: << pipeline.project.slug >>/deploy
          requires:
            - ok-to-deploy
          context:
            - devex-release
            - macos-codesigning

      - docs-publish:
          serial-group: << pipeline.project.slug >>/docs-publish
          requires:
            - ok-to-deploy
          context:
            - devex-release

      - smoke-test:
          name: smoke-test-snap
          executor: linux
          install-steps:
            - run:
                name: Install snapd
                command: sudo apt update --yes && sudo apt install snapd --yes
            - run:
                name: Install circleci via Snap stable channel
                # /snap/bin has to be prepended, not just present: the machine
                # image ships its own circleci in /usr/local/bin, which would
                # otherwise shadow the snap and make this job verify the build
                # agent's CLI instead of the release.
                command: |
                  sudo snap install circleci
                  echo 'export PATH="/snap/bin:$PATH"' >> "$BASH_ENV"
          requires:
            - deploy
          filters:
            branches:
              only: main

      - smoke-test:
          name: smoke-test-brew
          executor: macos
          install-steps:
            - run:
                name: Install circleci via Homebrew preview tap
                command: |
                  brew update
                  rm -f /opt/homebrew/bin/circleci
                  brew install circleci-public/circleci/circleci@next
          requires:
            - deploy
          filters:
            branches:
              only: main

      - smoke-test-docker:
          matrix:
            parameters:
              executor:
                - linux
                - linux-arm
          requires:
            - deploy
          filters:
            branches:
              only: main

      - smoke-test:
          name: smoke-test-choco
          executor: windows
          install-steps:
            - run:
                name: Install circleci via Chocolatey
                command: choco install circleci-cli -y
          requires:
            - deploy
          filters:
            branches:
              only: main

toolCalls.output:
Trigger, watch, approve and cancel runs, and list artifacts

## Usage

`circleci run <command> [flags]`

## General Commands

| Command | Description                    |
| ------- | ------------------------------ |
| `list`  | List recent runs for a project |

## Targeted Commands

| Command     | Description                                           |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `approve`   | Approve an approval job that is on hold               |
| `artifacts` | List and download the artifacts of every job in a run |
| `cancel`    | Cancel a run                                          |
| `get`       | Get a run's status                                    |
| `open`      | Open the current project's runs page in the browser   |
| `trigger`   | Trigger a new run of a pipeline                       |
| `watch`     | Watch a run until it completes                        |

## Flags

Global flags: `-c, --config`, `--debug`, `--no-color`, `-q, --quiet` — see `circleci --help`.

## Details

Work with CircleCI runs.

A run is one execution of a pipeline, created each time a trigger
fires. It carries the VCS context for that firing and groups the
workflows it produced; each workflow in turn contains jobs.

Inspect a job's details, output and artifacts

## Usage

`circleci job <command> [flags]`

## Targeted Commands

| Command          | Description                            |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `artifact`       | List or download artifacts for a job   |
| `get`            | Get job details                        |
| `open`           | Open job in browser                    |
| `output`         | Work with job step output              |
| `resource-usage` | Work with a job's CPU and memory usage |

## Flags

Global flags: `-c, --config`, `--debug`, `--no-color`, `-q, --quiet` — see `circleci --help`.

## Details

Work with CircleCI jobs.

Jobs are the individual units of work within a workflow.

Inspect, rerun and cancel workflows (job graphs)

## Usage

`circleci workflow <command> [flags]`

## General Commands

| Command | Description                             |
| ------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `list`  | List workflows for a run or recent runs |

## Targeted Commands

| Command  | Description               |
| -------- | ------------------------- |
| `cancel` | Cancel a running workflow |
| `get`    | Get workflow details      |
| `open`   | Open workflow in browser  |
| `rerun`  | Rerun a workflow          |

## Flags

Global flags: `-c, --config`, `--debug`, `--no-color`, `-q, --quiet` — see `circleci --help`.

## Details

Work with CircleCI workflows.

Workflows orchestrate jobs within a run. Use these commands to
inspect workflow status, rerun failed jobs, or cancel a running workflow.

Workflow IDs are shown in the output of 'circleci run get'.

**`test-windows` takes the longest, and it sets the length of the whole workflow.** It runs for about 4m15s and, in both full runs I checked, starts roughly 2 minutes after the workflow begins. The workflow takes about 6m20s, and `test-windows` finishes last.

I looked at run `2b52002a` in detail, which ran the full `ci` workflow in 6m25s. I compared `test-windows` against a second run, `64e7fabe` (6m19s), and got nearly the same numbers.

| Job | Duration | Biggest steps |
|---|---|---|
| **test-windows** | **4m16s**, plus about 2m before it starts | `task ci:test` 2m25s · Go setup 1m33s · checkout 8s |
| dry-run | 2m03s | `task ci:build` 45s · Go setup 37s · snapcraft install 18s · choco 8s · apt update 7s |
| test-macos | 1m44s, plus about 50s before it starts | `task ci:test` 1m12s · Go setup 25s |
| test-linux | 1m43s | `task ci:test` 1m07s · Go setup 32s |
| check | 59s | Go setup 37s · `task ci:check` 18s |
| docs | 40s | Go setup 35s · docs build and link check under 2s |

**Why:**

1. **Windows is slow at every stage, not just one.**
   - **Waiting to start:** the workflow was created at 18:22:07, but the Windows machine didn't start spinning up until 18:24:13. My guess is it's waiting for a free `windows.medium` machine. The second run showed the same ~2m07s gap.
   - **Tests:** `task ci:test` takes about 2m25–2m31s on Windows, against about 1m07s on Linux and 1m12s on macOS. That's more than twice as slow.
   - **Go setup:** this step (setup-go: installing Go and restoring caches) takes 1m19–1m33s on Windows, against about 25–37s elsewhere. Restoring the Go toolchain alone takes 21–30s, against under 1s on Linux. Restoring the module cache takes about 34s, and there's an unexplained 13–20s gap between those two steps.
   - **Checkout:** 8–10s, against about 1s on Linux.

2. **Restoring the Go module cache costs about 25–28s in every Linux job.** `check`, `docs`, `dry-run` and `test-linux` each pay this before doing any real work. It's most wasteful in `docs`: about 35s of setup for under 2s of building the site. Saving the caches takes under 0.2s, so restoring is the expensive part.

3. **`dry-run` installs its tools on every run.** apt update, snapd/snapcraft and choco add up to about 33s before `task ci:build` (45s) even starts.

**What I didn't cover:**
- All 10 recent runs are on the `bench/sidecar-test` branch. The main-only jobs (`deploy`, `mark-release`, `docs-publish` and the smoke tests) haven't run there, so I have no timing data for them.
- The latest run (`6eed8b92`) is mostly reruns of `test-linux`, and one of them failed in a 7m10s workflow. I didn't look into that failure.
- I didn't check the Taskfile, so I can't tell you which tests make Windows slower.

**Possible next steps:**
- Make `test-windows` faster, for example by splitting or running in parallel the slow tests in `ci:test`, or trying a larger Windows machine.
- Look into why it takes about 2 minutes to start.
- Look into why restoring the module cache takes about 27s.
- Consider whether `docs` needs the full Go setup, including the golangci-lint cache.

I haven't changed anything in the project.
